requirements.note: Inset-grouped list with Pinned and Notes sections. Newest first. Bold title, then a date (time today, Yesterday, weekday, or M/D/YY) and a one-line preview.
Search field at the bottom filters title and body live, with a No Results empty state.
Title and body edit in place with no Save button. Going back shows the note at the top of Notes with today's time.
Compose opens a blank note with the keyboard up. Leaving it empty discards it (count unchanged); a note with text is kept.
Swipe left shows Delete. Long-press menu has Pin/Unpin Note and Delete. Swipe right has no pin action and opens the note instead.
'90 Notes' subtitle under the large title; it collapses into the inline title on scroll and updates on delete and create.
Edits, deletes, new notes and pins all survived a relaunch.

bugs: A rightward (leading) swipe on a row opens the note, as if it were a tap, instead of doing nothing or showing a leading action.
tells: The body placeholder 'Note' in an empty new note is tiny and oddly letter-spaced, unlike the Title placeholder above it.
Previews truncate early at a word boundary with space left ('Ask about podcast…' ends about two-thirds across) in some rows, character by character in others.
At the largest text size titles stay on one line and truncate ('Podcast…', 'Meeting…') instead of wrapping.
The 'No Results' empty-state title is regular weight rather than the system's bold.
Pin is only in the long-press menu and the editor, not among the swipe actions.
A.scroll: Smooth through the 90 rows: no blank rows, pop-in or jumps. Large title collapses properly, it bounces at both ends, and the scroll position is kept when returning from a note.

requirements.note: Laid out like Apple Notes: large title, search under it, inset-grouped Pinned and Notes sections. Newest first. Title wraps, then a relative or short date and a one-line preview.
Search filters title and body live. Bottom toolbar shows 'N Results'; the empty state is the standard bold No Results.
Title and body edit with no Save button (a Done checkmark only closes the keyboard). The edited note moves to the top of Notes.
Compose button in the bottom toolbar. An empty new note is discarded on Back; a note with text is kept.
Swipe left shows Pin and Delete, and a full swipe deletes. Long-press menu has Pin/Unpin and Delete. The editor's ••• menu has the same.
'90 Notes' centred in the bottom toolbar, as in Apple Notes. It updates on delete and create, and shows a result count while searching.
Edits, deletes, new notes and pins all survived a relaunch.

tells: The note count in the bottom toolbar stays small at the largest text size while everything else scales (minor).
Dates use a full four-digit year (9/27/2026) where Notes uses a short date; it costs preview width but is not wrong.
B.scroll: Smooth throughout: steady drag, flings that decelerate naturally, no blank or popping rows. The search field docks under the inline title on scroll, and the scroll position is kept on returning from a note.

why: Both apps meet every requirement and persist correctly. B is closer to a native Notes app: pin and delete in the swipe actions with full-swipe delete, a toolbar count and compose button, titles that wrap at the largest text size, and a standard No Results view. A has a few small tells (a tiny, odd body placeholder, uneven preview truncation, titles truncating at large text) and a leading swipe that opens the note by mistake.
